items.title: Keith Ingham interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: Otto Harbach wrote that to Kern’s wonderful melody.

ctx.x: And why did they last so long?

Why did they last long? Because they’re good. They’re good melodies, they express — maybe the lyrics can be a little silly, maybe some of them are dated — but sometimes they express eternal truths. A lyric like “Smoke Gets In Your Eyes” you know, you’re madly in love with somebody and they don’t return your love. “When your heart’s on fire/smoke gets in your eyes.” Beautiful. Otto Harbach wrote that to Kern’s wonderful melody. I mean that’s kind of still around. And I notice when I’m playing places, young people…
How can we expect them to get into something that they’re not exposed to?
